description: We are Cosmic Catalysts, a team working on the Flame in Freefall challenge. Our goal is to use AI to analyze microgravity combustion data and turn it into fire safety insights for Moon and Mars missions. We are learning Python, data analysis, and dashboard building. We're looking for teammates with skills in Python/pandas, Streamlit or web design, and presentation/storytelling. Passion for learning matters most. Everyone is welcome!
summary: Fire behaves differently in microgravity, and Moon and Mars habitats may use low pressure and extra oxygen. Our dashboard turns NASA ISS flame tests (PSI-159 and PSI-10) into a habitat fire risk simulator. Users pick a pressure and oxygen level and compare it with the 12 closest real tests. It also maps data gaps and ranks which conditions NASA should test next.
details: Flame in Freefall is an interactive dashboard that turns NASA's ISS microgravity flame experiments into insights for Moon and Mars habitats, where air pressure and oxygen may differ from Earth. What it does: Key findings and charts from 179 ISS flame tests (PSI-159), plus test conditions from PSI-10 (366 total). Habitat Fire Risk Simulator: pick a pressure and oxygen level and compare it with the 12 closest real tests. Coverage map that shows data gaps. Only 19 of 366 conditions are low-pressure and oxygen-rich (28 to 36%). Next-experiment ranking. Top suggestion: 0.50 bar and 28% oxygen. Cool Flame Finder: 7 of 179 tests showed cool flames, all 30% butane at 2.03 bar, matching NASA's final report.Key results: Flames burned about 13x longer at 32% oxygen or more (65 s vs 5 s). Earth-like air gave about 5 s, while 0.55 bar and 34% oxygen gave about 111 s. This is an association only, because fuel and flow rate were not controlled.
